summary: A cleaned CSV of all ~6,200 US Medicare-certified hospitals sourced from CMS Care Compare Hospital General Information dataset — publicly downloadable with no authentication required. Fields include hospital name, address, phone, hospital type (acute care, critical access, psychiatric, children's), ownership (for-profit, nonprofit, government, VA, church), emergency services flag, overall star rating (1–5 stars), mortality rating, safety rating, readmission rating, patient experience rating, timeliness of care rating, and CMS Certification Number (CCN). Definitive Healthcare charges $15,000–$50,000/year for hospital intelligence used by medtech, pharma, and health IT vendors; IQVIA charges even more. A $59 one-time Gumroad flat file targets health IT SDR teams, medical device reps, healthcare staffing agencies, and hospital consulting firms — the broadest and most commercially valuable segment of the healthcare B2B market — who need a bulk hospital contact and quality-ratings list that no affordable flat-file product currently sells.

audience.who: Health IT and EHR SDRs (Epic, Oracle Cerner, Meditech, MEDITECH, Altera) targeting acute care hospitals for contract renewals and competitive displacement; medical device and surgical supply reps (Stryker, Medtronic, Johnson & Johnson MedTech) who need hospital-level contact and ownership data for territory planning; healthcare staffing agencies placing RNs and travel nurses in acute care hospitals (targeting hospitals with low staffing ratings); hospital management consulting firms (Huron, Navigant, Quorum) prospecting for turnaround and quality improvement engagements; pharmaceutical companies targeting hospital formulary decision-makers by hospital type and star rating.

data_wanted: CMS Care Compare — Hospital General Information dataset, updated monthly. Download URL: https://data.cms.gov/provider-data/dataset/xubh-q36u. Fields per hospital: CMS Certification Number (CCN), facility name, address (street, city, state, ZIP), phone number, hospital type (Acute Care – General, Acute Care – Department of Defense, Acute Care – Veterans Administration, Critical Access Hospital, Psychiatric, Children's), hospital ownership (Voluntary non-profit – Church / Private / Other; Proprietary; Government – Federal / State / Local / Hospital District; Physician; Tribal), emergency services (yes/no), meets criteria for meaningful use of electronic health records, overall star rating (1–5, or 'Not Available'), safety of care rating, readmission rating, patient experience rating, effectiveness of care rating, timeliness of care rating, efficient use of medical imaging rating, mortality rating. No login or API key required — direct CSV download from data.cms.gov.

evidence.source: CMS Care Compare Hospital General Information — official public dataset, monthly updated, direct CSV download with no authentication required, ~6,200 hospitals
evidence.quote: Hospital General Information dataset provides comprehensive data on all Medicare-certified hospitals, including facility type, ownership, star ratings, and contact information. Updated monthly. Available as CSV, JSON, or API.

evidence.source: AHA (American Hospital Association) Hospital Statistics 2025 — confirms ~6,200 registered hospitals in the US, with approximately 2,600 nonprofit, 1,200 for-profit, and 1,000 state/local government hospitals
evidence.quote: Total US registered hospitals: 6,120 (2024). Community hospitals: 5,129. For-profit hospitals: 1,167. Nonprofit hospitals: 2,616. State and local government hospitals: 1,008. Critical access hospitals: 1,358.

willingness_to_pay.signal: The hospital data market is the highest-value segment in all of healthcare B2B: Definitive Healthcare has a $300M+ annual revenue business built on it, IQVIA and Sg2 charge similar enterprise rates, and every medtech sales rep, health IT SDR, and hospital recruiter uses some form of hospital directory. A $59 flat CSV with hospital names, addresses, types, ownership, and 5-star quality ratings captures the massive underserved long tail — solo medical device reps, healthcare startup SDRs, travel nurse agency recruiters, and boutique consulting firms — none of whom can justify $15K/year but would trivially spend $59 to build a call list. The quality ratings angle is particularly strong for staffing agencies (filter for 1–2 star overall hospitals = highest care quality pressure = highest staffing need).

first_sale_path.channel: Gumroad one-time download + LinkedIn posts targeting health IT sales leaders, medtech reps, and healthcare staffing agency directors + r/healthIT and healthcare LinkedIn groups + direct outreach to health IT startup founders and solo medtech reps on LinkedIn
first_sale_path.angle: Title: 'US Hospital Directory 2026 — 6,200+ Medicare-Certified Hospitals, Star Ratings, Ownership & Contact Info (CSV)'. Key selling points: (1) Every Medicare-certified hospital in the US — name, address, phone, hospital type (acute care, critical access, psychiatric, children's), (2) Ownership type — for-profit, nonprofit, government, VA, church — filter for your exact target segment in seconds, (3) CMS 5-star quality ratings — mortality, safety, readmissions, patient experience, timeliness — filter for 1-2 star hospitals (highest-need staffing and consulting accounts), (4) Direct from CMS public data — the same government source behind Definitive Healthcare's $15K/year platform, (5) One-time $59 instant CSV. Staffing agency angle: 'Find every 1-2 star hospital in your territory — those are your highest-urgency travel nurse accounts. 6,200 hospitals. $59 once.'
